doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: American promoters compared with French and Japanese
summary: American promoters are smarter, but French and Japanese ones treat artists almost artistically.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How would you compare American promoters to European or Japanese promoters, in terms of standards? You touched on the fees that are paid, but we know the gigs are more than just the fees, because there‘s a whole standard there.

Well, American promoters I suppose are better, because one thing, it‘s language. It‘s a language problem there. American promoters, because they‘re . . . I can‘t use that word now. I don‘t want to make myself a slicker, you know. I‘ve got more honesty in dealing with the promoters in Paris, but the American promoters are smarter.
Do you think they‘re more apt to meet your conditions?

Yeah. I can just talk about the French. The French and the Japanese meet all the conditions, but their approach to dealing with an artist is almost artistic, you know, rather than American promoters; bim, bam, thank you ma‘am, right? Black and white, business, you know, which that‘s what it‘s supposed to be. But it could be a little niceness somewhere.
